title: How a neural network learns
about: 3Blue1Brown's deep learning series as a rabbit hole. The main track goes from neurons to transformers; go deeper wherever the maths gets ahead of you.
description: A branching path through 3Blue1Brown's videos on neural networks: what a network is, gradient descent, backpropagation and transformers, with side paths into the linear algebra and calculus underneath.

track.title: But what is a neural network?
track.note: Start here: neurons, layers and weights, with handwritten-digit recognition as the running example.

deeper.title: Vectors (Essence of linear algebra, chapter 1)
deeper.note: Rusty on vectors? This is the picture everything else builds on.

deeper.title: Linear transformations and matrices (chapter 3)
deeper.note: Why one layer of a network is a matrix multiplication.

track.title: Gradient descent, how neural networks learn
track.note: The cost function, and how a network improves by walking downhill on it.

deeper.title: The essence of calculus
deeper.note: The intuition for derivatives that gradient descent depends on.

deeper.title: The paradox of the derivative (Essence of calculus, chapter 2)
deeper.note: What an instantaneous rate of change really means.

track.title: Backpropagation, intuitively
track.note: How the network works out which weights to nudge, and by how much.

deeper.title: Backpropagation calculus
deeper.note: The same idea with the chain rule written out.

track.title: Transformers, the tech behind LLMs
track.note: From recognising digits to predicting the next word: the architecture behind large language models.

deeper.title: Attention in transformers, step-by-step
deeper.note: The mechanism that lets each word look at every other word.
